### 2026-09-08 · 75M READ · test 3 BOOTSTRAP CONSISTENCY: mean TD residual +0.0072 [+0.0058, +0.0085] (late +0.0021 [−0.0024, +0.0062], NOT DETECTED), terminal |V − outcome| 0.0719 [0.0564, 0.0913] (0.3050 [0.2587, 0.3558] on decisive losses); trend over 4 cycles FLAT — reads as TARGET

Model-free read of `ai_v12_02_winprob_critic` `eval_traces` at **50000016 / 60000000 / 70000032 /
74000016** (the last = the run's final cycle at 75,005,952). Writeup + raw JSON:
`designs/research_state/measurements/winprob_critic_75M_read_2026-09-08/bootstrap_consistency.md`.
DESCRIPTIVE, no bar (registration `44e3a7f5`). Answers the open question the D2 VERDICT raised
(`6c4ae35d`): is the late optimism the γ = 1 terminal-label TARGET or a MOVING-POLICY target?

**Invariants asserted, not assumed, and exact on all four cycles:** γ = 1.0; **0** of 28,536
decisions carry a non-zero off-terminal reward; **0** violations of δ ≡ ΔV; terminal reward
`WIN→[1.0] / LOSS→[0.0]`. So δ_t = V(s_{t+1}) − V(s_t) exactly, and G(s) is the terminal win
indicator.

🚨 **THE METHOD IS THE RESULT: the registered discriminator is NOT EVALUABLE ON THE RAW TRACES.** The
tree is loss-enriched by design (`eval_manifest.selection_rule`: first 10 losses + 5 wins per
opponent), i.e. battles are selected on their OUTCOME — a FUTURE event — which breaks the martingale
property E[δ | V] = 0 *even for a perfectly consistent critic*. The manifest records per-opponent
`capture_rate_win/loss`, so every battle was reweighted by 1/capture_rate; **the weights validate —
the reweighted count is exactly 1400.0 = 14 opponents × 100 on every cycle**, and the win rate goes
0.463 captured → **0.821** population. Read raw, this test returns **the opposite answer with a
confident interval**: δ_late −0.0078 [−0.0130, −0.0034] (detected ⇒ "within-game drift ⇒ MOVING
POLICY"), overdispersion 1.73 [1.55, 1.92], skill **−0.116** against the base-rate cap. Reweighted:
δ_late NOT DETECTED, overdispersion **0.966 [0.855, 1.100]** (1.0 inside), skill **+0.258**. Every
number below is the reweighted read; intervals are a 2,000-resample cluster bootstrap over BATTLES.
This also closes the `calibration` CLI's own dominant caveat — its raw bias +0.3113 and
`critic_mean_reducible_upper_bound` **0.6284** are the loose bound it warns about; its stated
identity P(win)·bias_win + P(loss)·bias_loss = 0.8213·(−0.1651) + 0.1787·(+0.6354) = **−0.0220**
reproduces the reweighted bias **+0.0060 [−0.0319, +0.0501]** (NOT DETECTED) within its interval.

**(a) TD residual, 74M.** All +0.0072 [+0.0058, +0.0085]; early ≤10 **+0.0147 [+0.0126, +0.0166]**
(detected), mid 11–24 +0.0017 [−0.0003, +0.0036], **late ≥25 +0.0021 [−0.0024, +0.0062] — NOT
DETECTED**; bot +0.0113 [+0.0099, +0.0129], pool +0.0023 [−0.0001, +0.0041]. Sign runs 2.206 against
the iid reference 2.0, lag-1 acf −0.042 — no persistent one-way run. **The sharp instrument, E[δ |
V-level]** (conditioning on the PAST only, so 0 at every level under a consistent bootstrap): ALL
**+0.0182 [+0.0115, +0.0253]** at [0.40,0.60), **+0.0119 [+0.0085, +0.0153]** at [0.60,0.80),
**+0.0065 [+0.0034, +0.0095]** at [0.80,0.95), −0.0021 [−0.0042, −0.0005] at [0.95,1.01); BOT
+0.0300 / +0.0223 / +0.0123 / +0.0002. So the bootstrap is **not perfectly consistent — V drifts
UPWARD from mid-confidence states** — but the drift is at the extremes absent and, decisively, has
the **WRONG SIGN** to produce late optimism.

**(b) Calibration (Murphy, base-rate cap, overdispersion), 74M.** OVERALL Brier **0.1261 = REL 0.0019
− RES 0.0454 + UNC 0.1700** (p̄ 0.783), skill **+0.2582**, overdispersion 0.966 [0.855, 1.100].
**The bias FLIPS SIGN across the game and the flip is detected on the BOT stratum, the one that
carries the verdict** (the pool stratum ran under the greedy-vs-stochastic handicap): bot early
**−0.0960 [−0.1270, −0.0572]** (PESSIMISTIC) → bot mid **+0.0321 [+0.0039, +0.0672]** (OPTIMISTIC) →
bot late +0.0575 [−0.0112, +0.1842] (not detected, only 31 battles reach turn 25 vs bots); pooled
late **+0.0732 [+0.0030, +0.1611]**, early −0.0585 [−0.0946, −0.0147]. **This replicates test 1's
late-minus-early gradient in DIRECTION** (+0.167 [+0.086, +0.251] there) at roughly half the
magnitude once the population weighting is applied. Overdispersion covers 1.0 in every slice but
`bot/early` (0.713 [0.622, 0.826] — UNDER-confident). **Resolution is the defect: RES 0.0454 against
a base-rate cap of 0.1700 = 27% of the available uncertainty**; `bot/early` RES 0.0074 against a cap
0.0996. That is D2's G1 failure seen from a second instrument.

**(c) The terminal anchor — the largest single defect, and QUOTA-IMMUNE** (a within-class read; the
IPW and raw columns agree to 0.011). **On the last decision of a game it is about to lose the critic
still says it wins 30.5% of the time**: |V(s_T) − y| on decisive losses **0.3050 [0.2587, 0.3558]**,
against 0.0212 [0.0110, 0.0343] on wins (V ends 0.979). All 0.0719 [0.0564, 0.0913]; bot 0.0470
[0.0329, 0.0662]. The 0.5 crossing: in a lost game V **peaks at 0.860 around turn 12** and then
falls, and **21.7% of decisive losses (26.1% vs bots) end with V still above 0.5**, while **100% of
wins** end on the right side. "V rising then losing" is real — but it is carried by the anchor, not
by a late residual.

**TREND over 50M→74M: FLAT.** Terminal V(s_T) on losses 0.300 → 0.237 → 0.230 → 0.305; RES 0.040 →
0.034 → 0.043 → 0.045; skill +0.239 → +0.207 → +0.252 → +0.258; E[δ | V∈[0.60,0.80)] +0.0177 →
+0.0132 → +0.0147 → +0.0119, every interval clear of zero, no trend. The arm's own reweighted win
rate over the same window is flat-to-declining, 0.848 → 0.821.

**DIRECTION — TARGET.** Against the registered discriminator read literally: the "target" clause
(δ ≈ 0 at every bucket, with late optimism) holds in the buckets where the optimism lives — late and
mid both NOT DETECTED, late optimism +0.0732 [+0.0030, +0.1611] — and fails only EARLY; the "moving
policy" clause's own stated condition, δ ≠ 0 **late**, is **not met on any of the four cycles**.
Three positive legs: (1) **the optimism enters at the anchor** — V(s_T) = 0.305 on a loss is exactly
the γ = 1 undiscounted final label failing to drive a losing terminal state to 0, and with the late
bootstrap consistent it propagates back into every late state; (2) **the drift that does exist has
the wrong sign** — upward from mid-confidence states, with the head PESSIMISTIC early (bot −0.096),
which is the lag signature, but a lag cannot then over-predict late; (3) **a lag that does not shrink
when the thing it lags stops moving is not a lag** — the policy is flat-to-declining over 50M→74M
while the drift, the resolution and the anchor are unchanged. **What unifies every number is neither
hypothesis in its pure form: the head is COMPRESSED toward its own base rate** — V sits near
0.75–0.79 while the truth runs 0.814 early → 0.703 late, so one shrinkage reads as early pessimism,
late optimism, and a V(s_T) that cannot reach 0. The γ = 1 terminal label is the *reason* for the
compression (a single undiscounted 0/1 per battle is a maximally high-variance target and a head fit
to it under-fits toward the mean), so the direction stands as **TARGET, with the mechanism named as
UNDER-RESOLUTION** rather than "reads the material lead and over-commits".

**Contradicted the registration.** (i) **`td_resid_tails` is not a CLI and has no `--help`** — it is

### 2026-09-08 · BUILT · the privileged (true-team) value channel `--value-true-team` (gen3_value_true_team_v1) — arm 5 of the critic ladder; ARCH surface unchanged when OFF

**What it is.** A new Dict obs key `opp_true_team` `[6, POKEMON_FULL_DIM]` carrying the opponent's ACTUAL party — species, moves, item, ability, derived stats, current HP and status — in the observation's OWN per-mon layout, produced by the SAME `PokemonEncoder.encode` the flat vector's opp slice uses, called with `is_own=True` against the OPPONENT's own battle view (from that side every one of its mons is a fully-known own mon, so there is no second encoding to keep in step). `TrueTeamValueReadout` slices it with the SAME `slice_pokemon_categoricals` `ObsUnpack` uses, embeds through the SHARED tables, pools six rows permutation-invariantly (`TTV_K`=4 queries over `TTV_DIM`=64) and adds a ZERO-INIT `D_MODEL` projection into `value_pooled` through the `_value_pooled_routes` seam, which now has two members. This is the **only** route in the tree that adds INFORMATION rather than re-reading the shared observation both heads consume — the defect the ladder note's L1 audit named.

**The policy provably cannot see it, and that is structural rather than a convention.** `ProjectionAssembler` returns `vf_combined` **as** `value_pooled`, and `pi_combined` is a concat that never contains it. So `pi` is BIT-identical under an arbitrary perturbation of the privileged key at a LARGE random weight — not merely at zero-init — and a policy-only backward leaves the route's projection with zero gradient. Both directions are asserted on a real build (`true_team_value_test.py`).

**AUGMENTS rather than REPLACES the belief-keyed opp view on the value side, deliberately.** Replacing is the cleaner ceiling in the abstract and confounds two changes in practice: a null would then mean "privilege does not help" OR "the belief route was carrying the signal". Additive injection also leaves every existing value route bit-identical at init, and is the only form the seam admits.

**Presence follows the LOCAL sim, and nothing else.** `LocalBattleRunner` sets an `_opp_player` back-reference on both sides at attach time — the one place that knows both sides, so "the sim is local" and "the privileged key is available" are the SAME fact rather than two things a caller must keep in step. That covers bridge TRAINING, bridge EVAL (`eval_callback`: workers play in-process via `run_local_battles`) and `replay_counterfactual`. `Gen3Env` reads `battle2.team` directly and needs no handle. At ladder play (`main.play`, a real server) there is no runner, `RLPlayer` supplies the all-zero "unknown" block — the encoder's own ABSENT-slot spelling — and the policy, which never reads the key, runs unchanged. The route RAISES on a missing key rather than skipping (a silent skip reads exactly like a route that learned nothing — the gen-12 dead-tail bug).

**THE ARM IS READABLE, and this was the one thing that could have made it not.** Both critic meters take V and P(win) from the eval traces' npz, never from a re-forward — `cf_audit` reads `value`/`win_prob` off the recorded invocations, `main.critic_gate` reads `win_probs` off `eval_traces/step_*/<opponent>/*_states.npz` — so the V they read is the one computed AT EVAL, with the key, on the bridge. A channel present only during rollout collection would have had the arm measured on a V the run never trained; extending `RLPlayer` is what closes that. The prober's model-loading views, by contrast, REFUSE on such a checkpoint (`ProbeModel._pin`, one seam for all fifteen offline forwards): a V rebuilt from the recorded observation vector alone is V *stripped of exactly the privilege the arm exists to measure*, and returning it would chart a different quantity against the un-privileged arms. Model-free prober commands (`scan`, `triage`, `turns`, `falsify`, `calibration`, `loops`) are unaffected.

**ARCH SURFACE: unchanged, and not by luck.** The row is `family=Family.CRITIC` — the enum's documented case ("a new critic readout marks itself family=CRITIC … a guard that demanded they match the production mirror would refuse every critic arm it exists to protect"). The surface is DERIVED as `structural AND ARCH`, so the key set did not grow: `checkargs` on the arm's argv prints `✓ every ARCH-surface key matches the production mirror (39 of 50 registry toggles are the ARCH surface; 8 critic readouts + 3 non-structural rows are excluded by their own declaration)` — 39 before and 39 after. No existing argv's verdict moved, and turning the flag ON does not move one either. `designs/production_config.json` is untouched, which is correct: a critic that needs privileged inputs is not the critic that ships, so this is a CEILING PROBE and never production.

**Versioning.** `MODEL_CONFIG_VERSION` 113 → **114**; one STRUCTURAL bool gated by a bool compare in `check_compatible` (the injection is additive, so no width change downstream could catch a flipped flag); migration defaults a pre-v114 config to `False`, which is a record and not a guess. **NO `ARCH_SIGNATURE` bump** — the 2501-dim observation VECTOR is unchanged, no existing module moves, and the readout is built LAST, so an OFF run on this code is bit-identical to the same run on v113 and **every existing checkpoint still resumes**. That CORRECTS the design note's L1 prediction ("FRESH-RUN-ONLY … `check_compatible` will reject every existing checkpoint"), which assumed the channel had to widen the observation; the note's L1 section is updated in place with the correction and the audit preserved as written.

**Evidence that it works, all from this pass.** `--debug --steps 10000 --value-true-team` trains to `Training complete` on the rust bridge, with `[ModelVersion] Round-trip smoke test PASSED` and `model_config.json` recording `config_version 114` / `value_true_team true` (and `cli_args.value_true_team true`, so a flagless resume inherits it). A real bridge battle shows the emitted block carrying agent2's WHOLE team, strictly MORE mons than the trainee has revealed, a revealed mon's species-derived columns agreeing between the two views, and — the cheapest possible proof it is privileged at all — an ITEM the trainee cannot see. Two assertions in that test FAILED first and were corrected rather than relaxed: the item and the typed-Hidden-Power ids differ between the two views BECAUSE Gen 3 hides them, which is the channel doing its job. **Obs-build benchmark: no regression, and structurally none is possible** — the only `src/agents/observation/` change is a NEW module `encode` never imports. Measured back-to-back on a busy box: before 0.449 ms / 3 949 calls per encode, after 0.330 ms / 3 966, and a second after-run 0.453 ms / 3 727 — a run-to-run spread of ~6% on the load-stable metric, against a before/after difference of 0.4%.

**The arm's argv** (arm A's recorded `original_command`, `--pin-commit` removed, `--steps 10000000 --run-name ai_v12_14_ladder_truevalue`, plus the lever): `/home/goodlad/.claude/jobs/9ab51de6/tmp/argv_E_truevalue.txt`. `python -m main.checkargs --argv "$(cat …)"` → exit 0, 129 flags, **0 unrecognized**, clean ARCH SURFACE, `✓ this command still launches`. NOT LAUNCHED — the ladder's first pair (B then C) is registered ahead of it and this arm is the ceiling probe, to be run after B/C/D have located the residual.

### 2026-09-08 · INSTRUMENT · `main.ops.critic_read` — the critic ladder's registered read as ONE command (identity + G1 + turn-contrast, ARM − CONTROL with CIs and labels; refuses over silence)

**The problem.** The ladder registration (`2026-09-08 · REGISTRATION · THE CRITIC LADDER`) specifies a read that is three separate agent efforts per arm — today's tests 1–3 at 75M took **2–7 h each** and produced three differently-shaped reports whose statistics lived as loose scripts in one session's temporary directory. Six arms at ~4 h of GPU each would have cost more agent-hours in READING than in training, and two arms read by two different scripts are not comparable by construction.

**What landed.** `python -m main.ops.critic_read <arm> --control <control-arm> --out <dir>` produces the whole registered read in one invocation:

1. Resolves both runs read-only through `utils.paths.main_models_dir()` (`main.ops.run_ref`), and picks each run's **last COMPLETE eval cycle**. Complete = `eval_manifest.json` exists **and carries its `selection` block** — the manifest is written *before* a single battle is played with `selection: null` and PATCHED at COLLECT (`eval_callback.record_eval_selection`), so the manifest alone (rule 16's letter) says only that the cycle STARTED. `--on-live {skip-newest,refuse,use}` decides what to do when a launcher for that run is still alive; live PIDs are read from `/proc` by exact `--run-name` / `--run-dir` token, never by a pattern that could match the tool's own argv.
2. **IDENTITY** — `cf_audit` on that cycle with **no `--checkpoint`** (ledger `1a1ad063`), `--impl rust`, `--states 800 --anchors 150` as flags with the 75M read's defaults, explicit `--out` under `<out>/identity/`. Then the readout: reproduction rate, bias `V − p̂` overall / by turn bucket (≤10, 11–24, ≥25) / by stratum (bot, pool), Murphy with the **base-rate cap** (RES/UNC), and the `corr(turn,V) − corr(turn,MC)` contrast — every interval a battle-clustered bootstrap.
3. **RESOLUTION** — `main.critic_gate` with `--parent v9_fold_parent --famine-comparator off --skip-meter` and explicit `--json`/`--md` under `<out>/gate/`. **A fresh arm has no parent**; the flag is only what the tool's argparse requires, the G1–G4 bars come from the committed calibration baseline, and the ladder / famine / **G7** sections that would use a parent are not reported. Strength is not read. (This is the same fresh-arm gap `g7_report` hit on arm 1 — sidestepped by not quoting a section a fresh arm cannot fill.)
4. **THE DELTA** — every quantity as **ARM − CONTROL** with the **difference of the two runs' INDEPENDENT battle-clustered bootstraps**, labelled `DETECTED` / `WITHIN FLOOR` / `NOT DETECTED` exactly as registered. `--floor-json` supplies the replicate floor; **absent, the report prints "NO REPLICATE FLOOR — deltas are NOT DETECTED unless their CI clears zero, and never DETECTED against a floor"** and every detection carries the qualifier *vs ZERO — NO FLOOR*. Arm 6 (`ai_v12_15_ladder_ctrl10M_b`) will supply the floor file.
5. **Output** — `<out>/critic_read.md` (the four headline deltas first, then the full tables, then every command and every path) and `<out>/critic_read.json`. `--ledger-line` prints the one-line QUOTE in the registered form, numbers only.

**REWEIGHTING — which statistics reweight and which do not, because three different selections stack here and conflating them is how test 3 first returned the opposite answer.** Every number is reported under all three, with the registered one starred:

| correction | what it fixes | where it applies |
|---|---|---|
| `pop` | `cf_audit` draws a STRATIFIED sample (decile × outcome × turn tercile, 4× boost on high-confidence-from-lost); recombined at the frame's own (decile, outcome) mass | the SAMPLER, against the trace tree |
| `ipw` | `1 / capture_rate(opponent, outcome)` from the cycle's `eval_manifest.json` — **RULE OF EVIDENCE 17** | the loss-enriched TREE, against the eval population. **The REGISTERED weighting for every bias and every Murphy term** (`pop × ipw`) |
| `raw` | none | the **turn-contrast only**, because arm A's committed `+0.3089 [+0.0828, +0.5101]` is the POOLED UNWEIGHTED Pearson pair and the ladder is compared against that estimand |

**Two places reweighting does NOT apply, stated rather than assumed.** (a) **The ANCHOR arm** — its frame is a CENSUS of the bot battles it draws from and its estimand is the offline REPLAY DRIVER's fidelity, not a property of the eval population; reweighting it would answer a question nobody asked, and none is applied. (b) **The GATE rows** carry no weighting column because the scaffolding gauge applies the capture-rate correction itself from the same manifest rates — there is no unweighted variant of a gate row. A stratum whose opponents the manifest cannot weight comes through at **weight 0 with its coverage printed**, never at weight 1 beside corrected rows.

**REFUSALS (exit 2, cause named, no partial table).** No manifest · a cycle that has not COLLECTED · no complete cycle at all · state npz without a `win_probs` column (`--allow-missing-winprob`, default 0.0 — this is the check that the privileged arm's channel was present **at eval**, since both meters take V and P(win) from these npz) · anchor reproduction below the label-trust gate (`--anchor-tolerance`, default 0.90) · a draw/timeout share above 25% (`--max-draw-share`) · a malformed floor file · `main.critic_gate` exiting 2 (overridable by `--allow-gate-refusal`, which then says in print that the G1–G4 rows are missing and why).

**Verification.** `src/main/ops/critic_read_test.py` — 42 pure-unit tests on synthetic input, no `models/` read: each of DETECTED / WITHIN FLOOR / NOT DETECTED planted in both directions with and without a floor (including the one that matters — a CI that clears ZERO but sits inside the floor is WITHIN FLOOR, not DETECTED); the delta interval must be WIDER than either arm's own; every refusal path; and the cache reusing only on a matching fingerprint. The promoted statistics reproduce the 75M read's committed numbers **exactly** from `identity_labels.json`: bias `+0.0965`, Murphy resolution `0.0476`, skill `0.166`, turn-contrast `+0.3089`.

**Two smokes on real data**, both under `/home/goodlad/.claude/jobs/9ab51de6/tmp/critic_read_smoke/`, nothing written under `models/`:

**Two smokes on real data**, both under `/home/goodlad/.claude/jobs/9ab51de6/tmp/critic_read_smoke/`, nothing written under `models/`:

**(a) THE ZERO-DELTA PLANT** — `ai_v12_10_ladder_vf15` read against ITSELF. **45 delta rows, all exactly 0.0, every label `NOT DETECTED`.** Headline:

The intervals are non-zero and that is correct: an arm resampled against an independent resample of ITSELF has a real sampling spread. Only the POINT must vanish, and it does — 15.9 s, entirely off the cache.

**Orchestrator's reading.** Two defects, one measured for the first time and one found in passing, and the second is the larger: the head under-uses information it CAN see (its own team is in the observation from turn 1) as well as information it partly cannot (who it is playing). That moves weight from the hidden-information levers toward the target/capacity levers, and it changes the first conditioning arm: an own-team code beside the opponent code, not the opponent alone. Before either is built, a linear-probe read decides the mechanism — whether the trunk DISCARDS the opponent/team signal the observation carries (⇒ an auxiliary decoding loss is the treatment) or the signal is simply not there early (⇒ a conditioning input is). ### 2026-09-09 · INSTRUMENT + AMENDMENT · the training-side VALUE SIDECAR lands (`377a5aa1`), eval traces keep every cycle (`b07c42bf`), and the critic ladder's remaining arms re-pin to `377a5aa1` with a 4× trace quota

**Why.** The owner asked (2026-09-08) whether we log and keep enough traces to help the value-function work. Three gaps: arm A's 10M traces were groomed by the 20-cycle default, so the ladder's registered A@10M comparator was never computable; the ladder reads are underpowered at ~200 traced battles a side (arm 1's read: every resolution delta leaning positive, every CI covering zero); and nothing had ever recorded the critic against its OWN training target — every probe reads eval battles, a distribution the head is not trained on.

**Landed.** (1) `--keep-eval-trace-steps` default **0 = keep every cycle** (was 20; ~55 MB a cycle, ~3 GB for a 75M run). (2) The capture quota is settable: `--forensic-win-quota` / `--forensic-loss-quota` / `--forensic-draw-quota`, defaults **5 / 10 / 5 unchanged**. (3) The value sidecar: `--value-sidecar {auto,on,off}` (auto = ON under `--critic winprob`), `--value-sidecar-fraction` 1/64, `--value-sidecar-seed` 0; once per rollout a seeded sample of buffer states is appended to `<run>/value_sidecar/rows.jsonl` — step, rollout, env, t, episode, turn, V, win logit, the back-filled target, opponent class, win margin, episode length, completeness, timeout. Overhead **19.3 ms median per rollout** (`value_sidecar_benchmark.py`), 0.016 % of a hostile 120 s rollout; a smoke A/B cannot measure it (the ON arm ran 6.5 s FASTER — smoke variance). Reader `python -m main.ops.value_sidecar_read <run>`: calibration by turn bucket / opponent class / outcome / step with the Brier decomposition and battle-clustered CIs; refuses on a run without a sidecar. No `MODEL_CONFIG_VERSION` bump (`model_config.json` is a weight-shape whitelist). Detail: `designs/training/value_sidecar.md`.

**Two findings from the build.** The `opp_class` label was declared only under the opponent-intent labels, so on a win-prob arm with no intent loss the by-opponent slice would have been EMPTY on exactly the runs the sidecar exists for — fixed at `gen3_env` (a label key the extractor never reads; 6 tests). And an opponent RATING does not exist at training time — bots are unrated and a snapshot's Elo is post-hoc — so the sidecar carries the opponent CLASS, not a rating column that would be null on every row; the conditioning arm's Elo input (mixture diagnostic §12) therefore needs a rating SOURCE built before it, not just a route.

**AMENDMENT to the ladder's registration.** Arms 3 (`cflabels`), 5 (`truevalue`) and 6 (`ctrl10M_b`) re-pin from `f3502568` to **`377a5aa1`** (no rust commit between them — the sim is unchanged; `d94de2e3` is included) and run with `--forensic-win-quota 40 --forensic-loss-quota 40 --forensic-draw-quota 10` (~4× the traces a cycle, ~200 MB a cycle) plus the sidecar. The read stays ARM − CONTROL with the control at the old quota: the raise tightens the arm's half of each interval and biases nothing. Arm 4 (`tdaux`, live since 2026-09-08 22:19) keeps `f3502568` and the old quota. All three argvs re-validated by `checkargs` at `377a5aa1` (0 unrecognized, ARCH surface = production mirror, launches). Tag: INSTRUMENT; nothing measured.

### 2026-09-09 · CORRECTION + SCOPE · `ctrl10M`-vs-`ctrl10M_b` is total run-to-run variance, not a "seed-only contrast"; and one replicate difference is a SCALE, never a significance threshold

Two amendments, both raised by the Training Run session. (1) **Correction to its own earlier record:** when `ctrl10M_b` was validated it was reported as a "genuine seed-only contrast" from a token diff (run name + `--seed 1001`) and a trace of `args.seed` to its one consumer (`model_build.py:795`). The configuration claim stands; the inference — that the pair therefore isolates the seed term — is withdrawn: the battle stream is not seeded (the rollout-1 divergence above), so the pair measures TOTAL run-to-run variance, environment included. That is the floor every lever delta actually carries, and the more useful one; it is not what it was called. (2) **Scope of the floor:** the pair is ONE draw of a difference — a single degree of freedom, a scale with no interval of its own. It can say a delta of 0.002 is inside the noise and a delta of 0.15 is nowhere near it; it cannot underwrite a marginal call. **The critic meters' bootstrap CIs remain the inference; the floor can only DEMOTE (a delta whose CI clears zero but whose magnitude sits inside the replicate difference reads WITHIN FLOOR), never PROMOTE — a delta is not DETECTED for exceeding the one replicate difference we happened to draw.** That is how `main.ops.critic_read --floor-json` labels (DETECTED / WITHIN FLOOR / NOT DETECTED), and this entry fixes the reading of those labels so the replicate difference is never quoted as a threshold. Tag: CORRECTION.

### 2026-09-09 · INCIDENT · MAIN's rust binaries were rebuilt from a deleted worktree and panicked at startup for ~1 h 45 min (01:30–03:15) — the dex data path is baked at COMPILE time

**What happened.** The equivalence-smoke agent, told it could symlink one worktree's `target/` to another's, built `sim_bridge` (01:30) and `search_driver` (03:03) INTO MAIN's `src/rust_sim/target/release/` from the detached worktree `gen3ai-wt/eq-old`, then removed the worktree. `src/rust_sim/src/dex/mod.rs:59` resolves the data directory as `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")/../../data/pokemon` — a path fixed at compile time — so both binaries carried `/home/goodlad/dev/gen3ai-wt/eq-old/...` and panicked on every start: `dex load failed (gen 3): read .../gen3ai-wt/eq-old/src/rust_sim/../../data/pokemon/gen3_species.json: No such file or directory`. **Found** when the `tdaux` read's `cf_audit` reported LABEL TRUST FAILED, 0/135 anchors, every replay `rc=101` — an instrument refusing correctly. **Fixed** 03:15 by rebuilding from main (`touch src/rust_sim/src/dex/mod.rs` then `cargo build --release --bin sim_bridge --bin search_driver`; verified by `strings` on the baked path and a live request). **Blast radius:** the live arm `tdaux` was NOT hit — its one periodic restart preceded 01:30 and a running bridge keeps its loaded binary; `cflabels`, launching at that moment, was warned to hold or check its child log; the first `tdaux` read (which had also picked `step_8000016` because the launcher process was still alive at 03:03 — `--on-live skip-newest`) is DISCARDED and re-run pinned to `--step 10000032`.

**Rules from it.** (1) Never build into, or symlink, MAIN's `src/rust_sim/target` from a worktree — a worktree builds its own `target/` or nothing. (2) A binary's data path must be checked, not assumed: `strings <bin> | grep gen3ai-wt` is the one-line test; the fix at the source is to resolve the data directory at RUN time (an env var, else relative to the repo root found from the executable, else the compile-time default) and to make `sim_bridge` / `search_driver` print the resolved path on `--version`. Filed as a backlog row (P1, infra — a rust change, so it waits for the sim's return from "todo" unless the owner pulls it forward); until then the launcher's pinned-worktree builds are the arms' protection and main's binaries are the offline instruments'. Tag: INCIDENT.

### 2026-09-09 · BUILT + REGISTRATION · critic ladder arm 7 `ai_v12_17_ladder_strata` — `--win-prob-strata-weight 1.0`, opponent-CLASS-stratified weighting of the win-prob BCE (`f871e79f`, MODEL_CONFIG_VERSION 115)

**The lever.** Over the rollout buffer's labelled rows, once per rollout: per opponent-class weight `raw_c = min(f_c^(−s), 8)`, normalised so the MEAN row weight is exactly 1 (the denominator stays N — `s` re-prices the MIX without rescaling the value gradient, otherwise the arm confounds "balanced the classes" with "raised the critic's step"); `loss = Σ BCE_i · mask_i · w_c(i) / N`. Default 0 = OFF with the loss BIT-identical (the helper returns None and the caller takes the original path). Requires `--critic winprob` (refused in `combination_checks`, so `checkargs` sees it). Recorded in `model_config.json` for provenance and flagless-resume read-back, never in `check_compatible`; pre-115 migrates to 0.0. Not a `flag_registry` row (that registry scopes to extractor toggles; this is a loss weight, declared in `arch_tables._COEF_MODULE → win_head`). ARCH surface unchanged, confirmed by `checkargs`. TensorBoard family `win_prob/strata_*` (weights, fractions, shares per class, entropy, `strata_active`, `loss` vs `loss_unweighted`). 40 tests, including the gradient itself: on a production-shaped buffer (10/90 bot/pool) the bot stratum's share of |∂L/∂logit| moves **0.099 → 0.441**. Routine gate green (10,278 passed).

**Two design findings that bound what the arm can move.** (1) **The vocabulary is the four `opp_class` codes (`bot` / `pool` / `stable` / `exploiter`), NOT per bot name** — the bot archetype and the pool snapshot's step are drawn per episode inside the opponent wrapper and never reach the observation (the sidecar declined the same column). So the lever balances the between-CLASS share and leaves within-bot heterogeneity in episode proportion; the head refit's between-cell share was measured over 14 opponents, so this arm can close at most the class part of it. Per-name stratification needs the opponent id plumbed into the buffer — the first thing to build if arm 7 moves the meters only part-way. (2) **The 8× cap binds at the production mix**: at ~10/90, `s = 1` asks for 10× and gets 8×, so the objective splits **44/56, not 50/50** — a 4.4× re-pricing with a bounded per-row weight. Both pinned by test and documented. Also: under `--debug` every opponent is a bot, so the family showed `strata_active 0` on the smoke — an absent family means OFF, `strata_active 0` means on-but-idle, which is what the live arm will show until its self-play pool seeds.

**Registration.** Argv `argv_F_strata.txt` = the replicate control's argv minus `--seed 1001`, `--run-name ai_v12_17_ladder_strata`, `--win-prob-strata-weight 1.0`; `checkargs` at `f871e79f`: 0 unrecognized, ARCH surface = production mirror, launches. **Pin `f871e79f`** — its delta vs `ctrl10M` crosses `f3502568→f871e79f`; the first half is verified neutral, the increment `377a5aa1→f871e79f` gets the same pinned-input functional test before launch (dispatched; the Training Run session holds the launch for the verdict, and a non-neutral increment re-pins `ctrl10M_c` to `f871e79f` as the matched control). **Pre-registered read** at 10M by `main.ops.critic_read` v2 against `ctrl10M`: primary `cond.spread_ratio.t1_3` (control 0.1152) and `cond.own_team_r2.t1` (control ≈0) with the delta's CI clear of zero; secondary G1 resolution per stratum; the `win_prob/strata_share_bot` scalar must read ≈0.44 in the self-play regime or the lever was not live. Slot: after `ctrl10M_b`, before `truevalue`. Tag: BUILT · REGISTERED.

### 2026-09-09 · ROOT CAUSE · the rust-binary incident was `resolve_config`'s automatic `cargo build` through a worktree whose `target/` was a symlink to main's — not a hand-run build

Reframed by the Training Run session from the increment verdict's hazard, and accepted: the 01:30 and 03:03 rebuilds of main's `sim_bridge` / `search_driver` were two calls of `resolve_and_publish_sim_bridge_bin()` from `resolve_config` on a rust-bridge argv, made from the detached worktree `gen3ai-wt/eq-old` whose `src/rust_sim/target` had been symlinked to MAIN's (an option the orchestrator's brief offered). Cargo built from the worktree's manifest (baking `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` = the worktree) into main's shared target; the worktree was then removed. Nothing else needs to have gone wrong. **Three ingredients, all needed:** an automatic build inside config resolution; a compile-time data path; a shared target directory. Removing any one closes the class: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree (a worktree build physically cannot write into main's target), or a startup assertion in the binary that its baked data dir exists — failing with the fix, not a raw io error — or `resolve_and_publish_sim_bridge_bin` refusing to build outside the launcher. Filed on the P1 backlog row with the incident attached; not landed mid-ladder (tech debt, not an arm). Standing rules until then: never symlink main's `target/` from a worktree; set `POKESIM_SIM_BRIDGE_BIN` to main's verified binary before resolving a rust argv from any other checkout; `bootstrap.sh`'s optional cargo build in a worktree recreates the exposure exactly. The orchestrator's brief offering the symlink is the proximate error. Tag: ROOT CAUSE.

## 2026-09-09 · OPS · CRITIC LADDER — `ai_v12_15_ladder_ctrl10M_b` COMPLETE: the REPLICATE FLOOR exists (10,027,008 steps, 4.17 h, 0 crashes, G7 below bar on both halves)

The floor arm. Same argv as the control except the run name and `--seed 1001`, pinned
`377a5aa170bef8bf37be2af7217bb4d4f1b20b36`. Its job is not to test a lever — it is to say how far
apart two runs of the SAME configuration land, so that every lever delta in the ladder has a scale.

🚨 **IT IS NOT A SEED CONTRAST, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT.** `--seed` reaches only the SB3
constructor; it does NOT seed the battle stream, and two `--debug` smokes at the same commit and the
same seed diverge at rollout 1. So ctrl10M-vs-ctrl10M_b measures **TOTAL run-to-run variance** —
seed plus environment stochasticity — which is the right floor precisely because every lever arm
carries the same environment variance. An earlier description of this arm as a "genuine seed-only
contrast" was withdrawn: the argv claim was true, the inference from it was not.

🚨 **HOW THE FLOOR MAY AND MAY NOT BE USED.** It is ONE draw of a difference — a scale with a single
degree of freedom and no confidence interval of its own. It can **DEMOTE** a detection to WITHIN
FLOOR; it can **NEVER PROMOTE** one. A lever delta is not "detected" because it exceeds the one
replicate difference we happened to draw; the meters' bootstrap CIs remain the inference tool and a
delta's own CI must still clear zero.

### 2026-09-09 · BUILT + REGISTRATION · critic ladder arm 8 `ai_v12_19_ladder_lambda09` — `--win-prob-lambda 0.9`, λ-return targets in probability space for the win-prob head (`28ece02a`, MODEL_CONFIG_VERSION 116)

**The lever.** Per episode inside each rollout buffer, replacing the terminal back-fill: a row that ENDS its episode gets `G = y`; every other row gets `G[t] = (1 − λ)·V(s[t+1]) + λ·G[t+1]`, with `V` the RECORDED pre-update sigmoid win probability (`rollout_buffer.values` under `--critic winprob` is exactly that — not re-forwarded, so the target cannot move under its own gradient across the epochs). γ = 1 with a terminal-only signal makes the n-step return `V(s[t+n])`, so the λ-average collapses to one backward pass; the weight on the outcome at distance d is λ^d. Loss unchanged: BCE against the soft target (a proper scoring rule for the target's expectation). Default 1.0 = OFF, bit-identical by SKIPPING the recursion. Requires `--critic winprob` (refused in `combination_checks`). Truncated episodes: `--win-prob-lambda-truncated {bootstrap,mask}`, default bootstrap from the same `V(s_T)` SB3's GAE uses (fallback `V(s[last])`, counted) — those rows become LABELLED where today they are masked out (`lambda_unmasked`, 7–92 of 2,048 per rollout on the smoke, ≤4.5 %); an episode with no recorded outcome is never unmasked (computed from `episode_starts`, never inferred from `win_mask == 0`, which would anchor at a fabricated y = 0 — test-pinned). Composition: cf labels are disjoint (foreign recorded states, own labels, `win_target` untouched — losses add); strata weights rows and λ re-aims them — orthogonal. Recorded in `model_config.json` (`win_prob_lambda`, `win_prob_lambda_truncated`; the `td_aux_coef` class; pre-116 migrates to 1.0 / bootstrap; never `check_compatible`); `arch_tables._COEF_MODULE → win_head`; no `ARCH_SIGNATURE` bump. TensorBoard `win_prob/lambda_*`: `bootstrap_frac`, `weight_mean`, `target_shift` (mean |G − y|), `unmasked`, `loss` vs `loss_terminal` (same states, same recorded predictions — the difference is the target change, never a step of learning). 35 tests + a `combination_checks` row; routine gate green (10,373). Smoke at 0.9: `bootstrap_frac` 0.79, `target_shift` 0.26 → 0.13 over four rollouts, true bootstrap used; at 1.0: zero `lambda_*` tags, records 1.0.

**Three hazards for the read.** (1) `SIDECAR_SCHEMA` 1 → 2: on a λ arm the sidecar's `target` column IS the λ-return and `target_known` covers bootstrapped rows — an offline sidecar reader assuming a 0/1 outcome is wrong on this arm (header carries the λ fields). (2) The λ path has not run under `--compile-trainer` or the forkserver preload (it is numpy over the buffer plus one `predict_values` call the collector already makes, and adds no obs key — `--debug` cannot exercise that layer; the first two minutes of the launch are the test). (3) `bootstrap_frac` ≈ 0.79 at λ = 0.9 on ~30-step episodes — a strong dose; if the arm reads as instability rather than sharper conditioning, 0.95 is the softer rung.

**Registration.** Argv `argv_G_lambda09.txt` = the replicate control's argv minus `--seed 1001`, `--run-name ai_v12_19_ladder_lambda09`, `--win-prob-lambda 0.9`; `checkargs` at `28ece02a`: 0 unrecognized, ARCH surface = production mirror, launches. **Pin `28ece02a`**; its delta vs `ctrl10M` crosses `f3502568→28ece02a`, of which the first three increments are verified neutral and `f871e79f→d11386dc` and `d11386dc→28ece02a` are under the functional test now (both dispatched; the Training Run session holds the launch for both verdicts). **Pre-registered read** at 10M by `critic_read` on the OFFLINE 400-game (and 800-game) cycles against the offline control: primary bot resolution (replicate pair ±0.007 at 400 games) and own-team R² t1; the turn-1–3 spread ratio reported against the replicate difference (0.066, run-noise); **the identity test (V vs its own Monte-Carlo continuation) is the GUARD** — bootstrapping propagates late-value bias backward, so the late-bucket bias must not worsen beyond the floor (0.10 replicate difference at 400 games); calibration against real outcomes (ECE) reported for the temporal-difference fixed-point bias; and `lambda_unmasked` checked first, so nothing is attributed to λ that the truncation branch could explain. Slot: after `ctrl10M_c`. Tag: BUILT · REGISTERED.

### 2026-09-10 · BUILT + REGISTRATION · critic ladder arm 9 `ai_v12_20_ladder_denseaux` — `--win-prob-dense-aux 1.0`, KataGo-style dense auxiliary targets on the value path (`46ca68ef`, `gen3_dense_aux_v1`, MODEL_CONFIG_VERSION 117)

**The lever.** A `DenseAuxHead` (`Linear(D_MODEL, 64) → ReLU → Linear(64, 25)`, zero-init output) over the SAME `value_pooled` the win head reads, built last and never called by the forward (the `CfEvidentialHead` contract), predicting for every state the episode's END-OF-BATTLE facts back-filled like the win bit: survival of each of the 12 slots (ours 6, theirs 6; BCE), each slot's final HP fraction (BCE against the soft target), and scaled turns-to-termination (`log1p(turns_left)/log1p(250)`, BCE against the soft target) — one loss family so one coefficient means one thing (MSE on [0,1] is O(0.01–0.1) and vanishes through a saturating sigmoid; the price is an entropy floor on the two soft terms, read through `aux_hp_mae` / `aux_turns_mae`). `aux_loss = coef × mean(the three masked-mean terms present)` — a mean of TERMS, so twelve survival outputs cannot outvote one; an entirely-masked block is dropped. KO counts are DERIVED (`6 − Σ survived` per side), published as meters, not predicted (a count cannot honour a per-slot mask). Slot order from `ObservationEncoder.get_team_list`, never re-derived. **Masking, a three-way AND:** the episode finished inside the buffer (the `win_mask` condition); terminal availability — an opponent mon NEVER revealed has no observed fainted flag or HP and is MASKED, never fabricated as "alive at full HP" (a label wrong in a direction); per-state visibility — opponent slot order is reveal order, so a not-yet-revealed slot is not scored (that would anchor a label to an all-zero feature block, this arm's own defect one level down); measured `aux_masked_frac` 0.30 on the smoke. **λ precedence:** the λ recursion names no `aux_*` key and must not — these are terminal facts, not returns (source-scan test); under λ < 1 the two coexist. **Versioning:** `dense_aux` (bool, derived from the coefficient) is STRUCTURAL in `check_compatible` (the head's params are the whole state-dict delta and no shape error would catch a flipped flag), a `flag_registry` row `family=CRITIC`, `requires=("win_prob_mode",)`; `win_prob_dense_aux` (float) is the `td_aux_coef` class, recorded, so a flagless resume inherits the dose and re-dosing is legal while adding/removing the head is refused — verified live; no `ARCH_SIGNATURE` bump (the obs vector, the modules and the forward are unchanged; three LABEL keys on the `win_target` precedent, none an `extra_obs_keys` row). TensorBoard `win_prob/aux_*` (coverage, masked_frac, the three losses, per-side survival AUC, HP and turns MAE, derived KO MAE) + `grad/dense_aux_share` (0 on the first update by construction — zero-init output kills the chain rule; a rollout-0 read would wrongly conclude the trunk is untouched). 36 tests incl. both directions of the pi-independence proof (bit-identical pi/vf at a large random head weight; the aux loss DOES move a trunk parameter) and the zero-init surviving SB3's orthogonal pass on a real build; routine gate green (10,448). Smoke: ON — the family present, `aux_auc_own` 0.62 → 0.83 vs `aux_auc_opp` 0.54–0.61, `grad/dense_aux_share` 0.0 → 0.226, config v117 with `dense_aux true`; OFF — zero `aux_*` tags; flagless resume from the ON checkpoint inherits. ⚠️ `--debug` bypasses the preload/compile/warm-start layer (the head reads no obs key, so the synthetic-obs sites are untouched — asserted by test — but the first two minutes of the launch are that layer's test).

**Registration.** Argv `argv_H_denseaux.txt` = the replicate control's argv minus `--seed 1001`, `--run-name ai_v12_20_ladder_denseaux`, `--win-prob-dense-aux 1.0`; `checkargs` at `46ca68ef`: 0 unrecognized, ARCH surface = production mirror (39 of 51 registry toggles), launches. **Pin `46ca68ef`**; its delta vs `ctrl10M` crosses `f3502568→46ca68ef`, of which everything to `28ece02a` is verified and the increment `28ece02a→46ca68ef` (which also carries the sidecar guard's writer changes) is under the functional test now. **Pre-registered read** at 10M on the offline 400/800-game cycles (sentinels pinned to 3) against the offline control and floor: primary bot resolution and own-team R² t1 (now with the within-team rows beside them), the opponent-axis spread ratio, the identity test as the guard; the arm's own dose meters `aux_auc_own` / `aux_auc_opp` / `grad/dense_aux_share` quoted at each 2M line. **Slot:** after `truevalue` → `lambda09_b` (the replicate of the candidate) → `denseaux`. ### 2026-09-10 · PRE-REGISTRATION · hypothesis (C) SHRINKAGE for arm 8, its calibration-slope test with the three geometry guards, and the λ DOSE CURVE {1.0, 0.95, 0.9} with its direction fixed before any read

**(C), named by the Training Run session and adopted.** A λ-return target blends bootstrapped V into the label, compressing the target toward the base rate relative to the raw 0/1; fitting a compressed target is a SHRINKAGE estimator — variance down, rank order can improve, emitted amplitude falls. That is "alignment up, amplitude down" (own-team R² +0.15 with the between-team spread 0.16 vs 0.26–0.41), which neither (A) nor (B) anticipated because both were about WHERE information goes, not the estimator's scale. **The test** (tool v5, being built): the Cox recalibration pair — the weighted logistic slope of the realized outcome on logit(V) with its intercept (slope 1 / intercept 0 = calibrated; slope > 1 = UNDER-dispersed, i.e. shrunk), overall, on turns 1–3, and WITHIN the five team-strength strata (across- and within-team shrinkage are different things; (C) predicts both above 1). **Verdict rule:** SUPPORTED = arm 8's slope > 1 and above every control by more than the wider floor draw, CI clear; NOT SUPPORTED = near the controls with the spread still down — and then (C) is DROPPED, not replaced by a fourth story; UNREADABLE if the slope's own replicate floor swallows it. **Three geometry guards, because the slope's standard error scales as 1/SD(x) and (C)'s own prediction is that the arm's SD(logit V) is SMALLER — the arm's CI is wider by construction, a conservative bias that must be visible:** (1) SD(logit V) and SD(V) printed per side beside the row; (2) a COMMON-SUPPORT companion — both sides restricted to the overlapping range of predicted probabilities and re-estimated — removing the lever-arm difference by construction; (3) the slope's replicate floor printed as its own line beside the CI. A NOT SUPPORTED is written only if the common-support row and the SD line show the arm was not merely underpowered by its own effect.

**The dose curve, fixed now.** Under (C) the softer rung `--win-prob-lambda 0.95` is a DOSE prediction, not another lever: less shrinkage ⇒ calibration slope CLOSER to 1 than 0.9's, own-team alignment gain SMALLER than 0.9's, between-team spread LARGER than 0.9's. **The claim is a MONOTONE dose–response across {1.0 (the controls), 0.95, 0.9} on those three rows; a non-monotone result REFUTES (C) rather than being explained.** Three points on a dose curve is the object, not two arms with a story. The 0.95 arm is registered as `ai_v12_22_ladder_lambda095` (arm 8's argv with `--win-prob-lambda 0.95`, pin `28ece02a`), sequenced AFTER `lambda09_b` (the replicate, which prices the run-level floor on these rows first) and `denseaux`; launched only if (C) is SUPPORTED or UNREADABLE-but-consistent on the offline frames — if (C) is NOT SUPPORTED the 0.95 rung is not a dose test and needs its own registration. Tag: PRE-REGISTRATION.

### 2026-09-10 · RE-SPECIFICATION + RULE 18 · the λ dose curve is restated on its SURVIVING rows before `lambda095` runs; (C) is a cleaner test than proposed; own-team R² is never read on live frames again

Raised by the Training Run session, accepted on all three. **(1) The dose curve had a dead component.** It was registered as monotone across {1.0, 0.95, 0.9} on three quantities jointly, one of which — the own-team ALIGNMENT gain — was just withdrawn as a thin-frame artefact. Carrying it forward would test a dead quantity or let two-of-three read as confirmation. **Restated on the rows that replicated at both offline frame sizes:** monotone across {1.0 (controls), 0.95, 0.9} on the **between-opponent spread ratio** (larger at 0.95 than at 0.9) and on the **calibration slope** (nearer 1 at 0.95 than at 0.9); **bot resolution / resolution-all REPORTED beside them, NOT a monotonicity requirement** (its own 400-vs-800 disagreement, +0.002 then +0.010, says it is not stable enough to carry a registered prediction). Two components; non-monotone on either REFUTES (C). **(2) (C) is cleaner than proposed.** It was "alignment up AND amplitude down = shrinkage buying ordering by paying amplitude". Alignment up is gone. What survives — amplitude down, resolution up, skill up, calibration the best of any run — is shrinkage that removed mostly NOISE: textbook beneficial bias–variance, not a trade. So the slope read is decisive in a way it was not: **slope ≈ 1 with lower spread and higher resolution ⇒ the critic simply got BETTER; slope > 1 ⇒ the shrinkage overshot and the amplitude loss is a genuine defect.** There is no middle story. **(3) RULE OF EVIDENCE 18, banked beside rule 17:** own-team R² of V has produced THREE spurious detections in this campaign — `cflabels`' +0.084 (trace-frame asymmetry), arm 8's live +0.15 (thin loss-enriched frames), and it is the row whose eval-draw variance (±0.02–0.03) exceeds its own CI (±0.015). Three failures on one row is a property, not luck: a leave-one-battle-out decode target over 719 teams is unstable on any frame with few battles per team, and the controls reading ≈ 0 is itself the tell — a genuinely-zero row and a too-noisy-to-estimate row look identical. **Own-team R² is NEVER read on live frames; it needs ≥ 2 offline full-capture draws or it is not a measurement.** Tag: PRE-REGISTRATION · RULE.

### 2026-09-10 · INSTRUMENT + READ · the CALIBRATION SLOPE is BUILT (`main.ops.calibration_slope`, tool v5) and answers the pre-registration on the LIVE frames: arm 8's slope is **1.58 pooled / 1.43 at turn 1–3 — well ABOVE 1**, the highest of all eight 10M runs, and the only arm with a positive pooled delta (12/12 deltas positive) — the OVERSHOOT reading in LEVEL; but the DELTA is inside the live replicate floor (0.20 / 0.22), so the comparative claim is **UNREADABLE at 100 games** and the decisive read is the offline 400/800 frames. The frame-sensitivity declaration was CHECKED at a 6.3× frame cut and holds

**What this answers.** The instrument the *PRE-REGISTRATION · hypothesis (C)* entry above specified, built to that specification including all three geometry guards, and read. 🚨 **It was built and run in parallel with the offline READ and the RE-SPECIFICATION above, so its framing was the pre-registered one (*alignment up, amplitude down*) — the alignment half has since been WITHDRAWN and the rows below are re-read against the RESTATED (C):** amplitude down + resolution up + the best calibration of any run is shrinkage that removed mostly NOISE, and the slope is decisive with no middle story — **slope ≈ 1 ⇒ the critic simply got BETTER; slope > 1 ⇒ the shrinkage OVERSHOT and the amplitude loss is a genuine defect.** The quantity: `logit P(y=1) = a + b·logit(V)` (Cox 1958 recalibration), **`b > 1` = UNDER-dispersed (SHRUNK)**, `b < 1` over-dispersed.

**Built** (`src/main/ops/calibration_slope.py`; seven declared `Meter`s): the pooled and turn-1–3 slope + intercept, the WITHIN-own-team-STRATUM slope (a shared slope with a free intercept per stratum; a stratum with no outcome variation is DROPPED, not fitted), and the COMMON-SUPPORT pair. Weighted Newton/IRLS, HT-reweighted, `V` clipped at 1e-3 with the clipped SHARE reported, battle-clustered bootstrap within opponent cells, **NaN — never a diverging coefficient — on separation or one outcome class.** 🚨 **The slope's SE scales as `1/sd(logit V)`, and (C)'s own prediction is that the arm's is the smaller one, so the arm is handed the wider interval BY THE EFFECT UNDER TEST.** Two answers ship with it and neither is optional: the per-side `sd(V)` / `sd(logit V)` / support / clipped-share table printed beside the rows like the cell census, and the COMMON-SUPPORT companion (both sides re-fitted on the intersection of their central 95% of `V`, where the lever arm cannot differ; disjoint masses are REFUSED, not widened). A third `Meter` flag, **`pair_level`**, was added for it: the window names both sides, so `critic_read` fits that row from each side's CACHED per-state columns and a single-run block never emits it.

**The read** (10M, live cycles, quota-matched, floors = the wider of the two control-vs-control draws, regenerated on v5):

**Verdict, in the two halves the restated (C) needs kept apart.** **(i) LEVEL — arm 8's slope is NOT ≈ 1.** It reads **1.579** pooled and **1.426** at turn 1–3. At turn 1–3 the three controls sit at 0.76 / 0.80 / 0.98, i.e. correctly dispersed early, and the arm does not: on its face that is the OVERSHOOT branch of the rule, not the "simply got better" branch. Over all states every head reads above 1 (1.12–1.58) — the population is shrunk late whatever λ is — so the pooled level cannot separate the arm from an era-wide defect and only the turn-1–3 contrast carries the level reading. **(ii) DELTA — UNREADABLE at 100 games.** Twelve of twelve slope deltas are POSITIVE; arm 8 has the highest slope of all eight 10M runs on both rows and is the only arm whose POOLED delta is positive at all. But the other seven runs span 1.12–1.44 pooled and 0.76–1.27 at turn 1–3, leaving arm 8 only +0.14 / +0.16 above the top of that range, and the replicate floor agrees: **no row's CI clears its floor on any pair.** **NOT SUPPORTED is not written**, per the registered rule: at turn 1–3 the arm's lever arm IS the smallest (`sd(logit V)` 0.442 against 0.573 / 0.573 / 0.693) so it may be underpowered by its own effect, while on the pooled row the COMMON-SUPPORT companion keeps the sign and magnitude (+0.24 / +0.28 / +0.42) — that difference at least is not the support. **Consequence for the dose curve:** the restated curve needs the slope MONOTONE across {1.0, 0.95, 0.9}; on live frames that row cannot support a monotonicity claim (its floor is 0.20 against a controls-to-arm range of 0.34), so **the dose test must be run on offline frames, where the floors on the surviving rows are 3–8× tighter.** 🚨 **These reads are LIVE frames.** Rule 18 (banked above) is specific to the own-team decode and does not reach a pooled M-estimator over ~1,400 states, but the caution it encodes does: the decisive slope read is the 400/800-game offline pair, and it is the obvious next call.

**FRAME SENSITIVITY — declared, then CHECKED.** A weighted logistic coefficient is an M-estimator whose expectation is the population coefficient at every frame size given correct weights: no held-out optimism, no unsubtracted noise, no threshold-selected cell set ⇒ `frame_sensitive = False`. Verified at the most extreme cut on this ladder: `ctrl10M`'s 8/12 cap forces arm 8's frame from 651 battles to ~104 (**6.3×**) and the four base rows move +0.087 / +0.118 / −0.143 / −0.171, **every one INSIDE its own as-traced 95% CI**; the control side of the `ctrl10M_b` pair moves +0.050 / 0.000 / −0.123 / −0.001. The **within-stratum** companion moves **+0.415, OUTSIDE** its CI — the threshold-selected-cell mechanism exactly — and it is the one calibration row declared `frame_sensitive` and quota-matched.
